items.title: [EMNLP26]  RIGEL: Self-Distilled Score Adaptation for Image and Video Captioning Evaluation
Python Decorators from Syntactic Sugar to Production-Grade Design Tool
items.summary: Python decorators are among Python's most powerful and elegant features. Although their syntax is relatively simple, their capabilities extend far beyond adding an @ symbol before a function or class definition.In this talk, delivered at Python Summit 2026, I explore how Python decorators work, how to build your own decorators, and how to use them effectively in production-grade software.We begin with the fundamentals, examining Python's support for first-class functions and understanding what actually happens behind the scenes when a decorator is applied. From there, we move on to more advanced techniques, including function-based decorators, class-based decorators, nested decorators, and decorators that accept arguments.The presentation includes practical code examples showing how decorators separate responsibilities, reduce code duplication, and improve software maintainability.We also explore real-world applications of decorators, including:Execution Time Measurement: Measuring function performance without modifying the original implementation.Logging: Tracking function calls, arguments, and return values.Caching: Improving performance by avoiding unnecessary repeated computations.RESTful Web Services: Understanding how FastAPI uses decorators to define API endpoints.Command-Line Applications: Exploring how Typer uses decorators to simplify CLI development.An important part of the talk focuses on best practices for developing reliable, reusable, and maintainable decorators. We discuss preserving function metadata with functools.wraps, supporting arbitrary function arguments using *args and **kwargs, following the Single Responsibility Principle (SRP), proper exception handling, documentation, unit testing, and type hinting.As AI increasingly generates software, understanding good software design becomes even more important. AI can produce code quickly, but evaluating its quality, maintainability, and correctness remains essential. Understanding decorators and the design principles behind them helps developers make better architectural decisions and work more effectively with AI-generated code.Whether you are already familiar with Python decorators or want to better understand their capabilities, these slides offer practical examples, implementation techniques, and design principles to help you write cleaner, more maintainable Python code.Code samples from the talk:https://tinyurl.com/pythonsummitdecoratorsMore articles, courses, and software development resources:https://lifemichael.comConnect with me on LinkedIn:https://linkedin.com/in/lifemichaelThank you to the organizers of Python Summit 2026 and everyone who attended my session! 🐍🇵🇱
